what: Film grain shimmers across the whole screen — four transparent sheets scattered with text-color dots (3.3% of the area) are swapped at 5 per second, tiled as a 600px (350px on phones) pattern and blended at .25 opacity with difference. It appears as a light grain on dark backgrounds and a dark grain on light paper, so the grain stays alive when the background changes. Clicks pass straight through to what is below.
ease: steps(1) — switches instantly with nothing in between

options.density: Share of area covered by dots, default .033
options.res: Horizontal pixels used to bake one tile, default 1000 — if larger than the pattern width (--fx-tile), dots become finer than 1px
options.ratio: Height/width ratio of one slide, default .563
options.look: If local, instead of being fixed to the screen it stays only inside the wrapping section (the positioned parent)
options.--fx-tile: Width of one pattern tile (css variable), default 600px — 350px on phones

from.where: shared.css·index.html .ny-grain (grain over every screen — original is four beige dot GIFs at 200ms, 600px · phone 350px, opacity .25, difference)

shared.js .hp-noise (original #bg-noise canvas — dots half and half on a screen-sized ImageData (Math.random() < .5) ten captured shots swapped every 1000/15ms, canvas opacity .05 · z 10 · no blending. The original dot color writes 0xff133645 as little-endian, which becomes brown (69,54,19), but the copy uses the skin’s ink black)
from.options: frames: 10; fps: 15; density: .5; res: window width (max 1600); ratio: window height/width · style --fx-tile: 100vw; --fx-opacity: .05; --fx-blend: normal; --fx-z: 10

note: With reduced motion, bake just one frame and stop. Dot color is read once when attached — change the skin and it attaches again (remove and re-add data-fx)
